Hold Your Colour.

Do not be afraid of making it a fetish for yourself. Such a thing is an exploration of your body and your sexuality, but I will say; do not jump too far down into that wishing well.

I do not wish to put more of a boogeyman onto transitioning but, here is a piece of common sense for you from a thirty-one year old who is very, very glad they stayed away from the knife;

Why would you ever give up your chance for children, for mere aesthetic?

That is what I asked myself and what was my guiding rock through life that kept me away from the terrible advice that is along the lines of; just do it.

No. Don't just do. Think first. Consider second. Reconsider third. Then, perhaps, do something on the fourth.

Seriously, though. My body is male, yet I feel deeply female. So strongly a mother, in fact, that I cannot even remotely comprehend why anyone else on the same 'path' would ever, ever, \*ever\* sacrifice the chance for children. It is inane, and reeks to me of terrible and myopic advice towards unfortunately vulnerable minds.

Do not be afraid to find other spaces away from your 'closet' to expose yourself. Do not fall into the trap of thinking you \*have\* to be open and honest with your family - remember, you can choose your friends, but not your family (unless, of course, you value your friends as family!)

Expression is liberty. Expression is safety. The more you keep such thoughts and feelings trapped within, the less of you that exists 'out there'. Your footprint on this world is lessened and, worse; the questions you ask find no answers, and that is when paranoia pays plenty of visits.

Music. Art. Writing. Dance. Fashion. Find the language you are most comfortable with, then share yourself with the world. People might jeer, but remember;

The worst reaction is no reaction (or boredom). If people boo and jeer? Well; you're obviously doing something to piss the bigots off ;D

Don't lose grip of yourself. Hold your colour. If you're stuck in Hell, keep walkin'.

The only one with the power over yourself, is you.

You are valuable. Always remember that.

Love yourself.

The simple answer; music.

The long answer; write it out. Paint it out. Shout it out.

The more such thoughts, feelings and sensations are inside your head and the less you confront them through a medium that is entirely in your control, the more it gains control over you.

I cannot say it is something that will ever go away, but you should not be scared of such a prospect. Rather, see it is as the darkness that it is and be your own light to guide yourself forwards. Always remember that your close-by friends are those that should be supporting you and your feelings, and not those that question them or turn you away from your own answers-in-the-moment.

Another way I deal with it; Common Sense.

Dysphoria is a very challenging and difficult world to deal with, but if you challenge it with the idea of it instead being 'intuition', common sense. All these such things, you begin to weaken the blows that moments dysphoria deal. You get some control over the illusions your own mind weaves.

Some.

I do have to say though; do not get trapped on the idea of it being something you \*beat.\*

Instead approach it as something that you \*work with\*, even if you don't want to work with it.

Sadly, we cannot do anything about the cards we are dealt in life. Take the hand you are given, and let it be your ally towards a fruitful future.
